title: Outgrown Canva for Facebook Ads? When to Hire a Creative Agency
summary: Outgrown Canva for Facebook ads? Learn when a creative agency is worth hiring, what to brief, and which providers publish weekly volume and prices.
body_markdown:
Yes, hire a creative agency once the bottleneck is new concepts, finished video and test volume rather than layout. If one person can still make and approve every ad you test, a design tool and a steady brief may be enough. Knowlify is our top pick for done-for-you finished AI video ads on Facebook and Instagram. Knowlify publishes this guide and sells one of the services compared.


## Signs the bottleneck is creative, not design


The clearest sign is a test calendar that slips because nobody has time to make a new idea. A layout change does not fix that. Look at your last few months of ads and count how many are genuinely new concepts. Meta's creative diversification post treats two ads with identical visuals and different text calls to action as iteration, and it recommends ads that differ in look, feel, storyline and message ([Meta creative diversification](https://www.facebook.com/business/news/demystifying-creative-diversification) ). If most of your output is text or hook swaps on one idea, you have a volume problem.


Volume matters more on Meta now. Its Andromeda engineering post says the number of ad creatives in its recommendation systems is expected to grow significantly as advertisers adopt generative AI tools, and that the retrieval stage narrows tens of millions of candidate ads to a few thousand ([Meta engineering](https://engineering.fb.com/2024/12/02/production-engineering/meta-andromeda-advantage-automation-next-gen-personalized-ads-retrieval-engine/) ). Meta's Advantage+ page says its end-to-end campaigns automatically apply AI across a campaign's audience, placements and budget ([Meta Advantage+](https://www.facebook.com/business/ads/meta-advantage-plus) ). In our reading, that leaves the ads you supply to carry more of the work, so a monthly refresh can fall short when competitors ship more ads.


## Four questions to answer before you request a quote


1. **How many distinct concepts do you need each week?** Count concepts separately from hook and text variants.
2. **Which shapes and formats?** Meta's video ads guide lists a 4:5 ratio at 1440 x 1800 pixels for Facebook Feed, with captions and sound optional but recommended ([Meta video ads guide](https://www.facebook.com/business/ads-guide/video) ). Ask which shapes are included in the price, because a single master rarely covers every placement.
3. **Who approves each concept, and how fast?** Name the approver before the first brief.
4. **Which files do you keep?** Ask for source files, not only exports.


Our[video ad campaign brief](https://knowlify.com/articles/video-ad-campaign-brief) gives a structure to fill in before any provider sees the work.


## Knowlify: our top pick when Canva-built ads need to become weekly video


Knowlify is the best fit when the next step after Canva is a steady supply of finished video, not another tool for your team to learn. It makes about 25 finished AI video ads a week, the first batch lands on day 5, and a person checks every ad before delivery. Its three formats cover the jump from static layouts: AI UGC with AI presenters talking to camera, 3D and stylized character animation, and AI commercials. Our[AI UGC service page](https://knowlify.com/ai-ugc-ads) explains the presenter format.


The scope matches where you are now. If you already have someone running Meta campaigns, buy creative only. If not, Knowlify also offers end-to-end Meta campaign management. Pricing is a custom quote with no public rate card, and the guarantee covers the first 90 days: if the ads have not made more than you paid, you can cancel by email for a full refund (terms on the[pricing and guarantee section](https://knowlify.com/meta-ads-agency#pricing) ). That 90-day refund applies to creative-only plans; where Knowlify runs the account, the guarantee is an agreed target in 30 days, or you don't pay for the month.


When to pick another option: Knowlify does not supply real human creators or static banners at scale, so a brand whose ads depend on real customer footage or a large static library should shortlist a creator agency or a static-focused subscription instead.


## Agency or subscription: which fits your volume?


Published prices and output vary widely, so match each option to the output you need each week, not to the headline monthly fee.


Option Output Published price Caveat


Knowlify (our top pick) About 25 finished AI video ads a week, with a person checking each ad From $5,000 a month Makes AI presenter, animation and AI commercial ads, not real creator footage


[CreatStrat](https://creatstrat.com/) 5, 10 or 20 ads a week, with statics, carousels, footage mashups and AI video $299, $499 or $899 a month No revision policy or person-review statement on the page


[Adguns](https://adguns.com/service/weekly-creatives/) Typical weekly batch of 10 to 30 concepts plus resizes From €1,000 a month Media buying not included; first batch typically within 2 weeks


[Vidful](https://vidful.co/) 60 videos a month on its entry plan, with 20 concepts $3,495 a month Unlimited revisions; first creatives by the end of week one


[MetaAdsAgency](https://metaadsagency.com/services/creative-testing) 12, 30 or 60 new creatives a month by plan, with testing and media buying From $2,400 a month, billed yearly Works as a partner in your Business Portfolio


[Darkroom](https://darkroomagency.com/) 250 to 600 production-ready assets per cycle From $1,500 a month, plus a percentage of media Stated fit is typically $10M to $500M in revenue


Adguns and CreatStrat sell a weekly rhythm at a fixed price, which suits a team that already has a brief and a named approver. MetaAdsAgency bundles creative, testing and media buying in one fee, so it suits a team that wants one provider to run the tests.


Darkroom states its fit as typically $10M to $500M in revenue, and it calls companies under roughly $5M a poor fit. If your business is smaller, a larger agency may not be the right size, whatever its output.
